display_name: The Prevention of Corruption Act 1960: the offences, the presumption, the penalties, the powers of arrest, investigation and search, the evidence rules and the procedure (Parts 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and ss 3 and 4)
scope: Every operative provision of Parts 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6, and ss 3 and 4 of Part 2, of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1960 as printed in SSO's PDF, current version as at 01 Oct 2026: the offences (ss 5 to 12, 18(2), 21(2), 26, 28, 32(2)), abetment, attempt and conspiracy (ss 29 to 31), the presumption of s 8 and the deeming of s 9, the penalty rules (ss 7, 13, 14), the powers of arrest, investigation and search (ss 15 to 22), the evidence rules (ss 23 to 25, 36), and the procedural sections (ss 32 to 35, 37); and a statement to the Criminal Procedure Code 2010 about the Act's offences (ss 32(1), 34). NOT encoded: ss 4A to 4F (the Occupational Superannuation Scheme of CPIB officers); the Criminal Procedure Code's own rules for an arrestable offence, bail, warrants and investigation (sg/criminal-procedure-code-2010); the elements of the Penal Code offences the Act names (sg/penal-code-1871).

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act, and no independent test pass has been run: the tests were written from the Act's text by the session that wrote the rules. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. NOTES.md sections 7 and 8.

forks.F1: 'corruptly' is not defined by the Act and is a fact about the accused.
forks.F2: s 8: the presumption supplies the corrupt element and the purpose limb of ss 5 and 6, not that the thing is a gratification or was paid; its outcome is a BOOLEAN input to each offence rule.
forks.F3: s 9: the four 'notwithstanding' facts are fields so that a test shows they are not read.
forks.F4: s 3(3), (4): deputy and assistant directors are read as able to exercise the powers of the Director and of a special investigator.
forks.F5: The Act draws three lists of Penal Code sections (ss 17(1)(a) and 28(a); ss 20, 21, 22, 24, 35); they are kept as two constants and not merged.
forks.F6: s 7 raises only the imprisonment ceiling, from 5 to 7 years; the fine ceiling is $100,000 in both.
forks.F7: s 13(1): 'committed by the acceptance of any gratification' is read as ss 5(a), 6(a), 10(b), 11(b), 12(b).
forks.F8: The statement to the Code says the Act deems its offences arrestable (s 32(1)) and does not empower the police itself (s 15(1) empowers the Director and special investigators).
forks.F9: s 21(1)(a) to (f): the threshold is encoded; the six kinds of notice are not enumerated.
forks.F10: 'public body', 'principal' and 'special investigator' are facts, not rules.
